commentaries.author: parimēlaḻagar
commentaries.text:
She is sulking and won’t be won over by his pleading, and he says this.

When trouble comes, if your own heart doesn’t help you, no one else will. The trouble here is that her sulk won’t yield to his pleading. His heart fails him by longing for union, instead of deciding she has no loving-kindness and giving her up. With no help at all, he can only bear it and let it go.
